name: Schad v. Arizona
summary: A plurality held that the Constitution does not require jury unanimity on the theory of guilt when multiple theories are submitted as alternative means of committing a single crime, rather than as separate elements.
significance: A closely divided Court upheld a murder conviction where jurors may have disagreed on whether the defendant committed premeditated murder or felony murder, and both sides invoke it to support their competing visions of what the Constitution requires regarding juror agreement.
